Context: this code is part of an internal service that processes files uploaded by customers. Inputs can be empty, very large or malformed, and the service runs many copies in parallel, so correctness under bad input matters more than raw speed. Reviewers on this team expect clear names, small functions and no hidden global state.

Review this code as if it were a pull request. List bugs, risks and style problems, most serious first.

```sql
SELECT c.name, SUM(o.total) AS spent
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
WHERE o.status = 'paid'
GROUP BY c.name
ORDER BY spent DESC
LIMIT 10;
```

Anything that can fail silently should fail loudly instead, with a message that tells the reader what to check first.
